title: Perguntando sobre a volta
grammar: Can we…? para perguntar por uma opção conjunta
reading: Rob and May are at the ticket desk in the city.
They are brother and sister, and it is a family trip.
They would like a round trip, not one way.
The fare is low, and they have money.
The return train is at six.
They come back on Sunday.
dialogue: Hello! Can we buy a round-trip ticket to Chicago, please?
Sure. Is it for Friday?
Yes, it is. Is there a return train on Sunday evening?
Yes, there is. It is at six. The fare is forty dollars.
That is fine. Can we pay by card?
Of course. Do you have a card, or do you have cash?
We have a card. Can we come back on Monday, too?
Yes, you can. Here are your tickets. Thank you!

title: A rotina no computador
grammar: Presente simples com I para falar de rotina
reading: I come to the classroom at eight.
I sit at my desk and open the computer.
The screen is blue, and I type my name on the keyboard.
I check my email before class.
I open a green folder on the screen.
Then I wait for the teacher.
dialogue: Hi Ben, is this your computer?
Yes, it is. I use it every day.
Can I look at the screen? It is blue.
Sure. I check my email here before class.
Do you have a mouse for this computer?
Yes, I have one. Here you are.
Thanks. Can I type my name on the keyboard?
Yes, you can. Please sit at my desk, and wait.

title: Organizando o material de estudo
grammar: He e she com a terminação -s no presente
reading: Mia sits at her study desk every day.
She uses a notebook for English.
Her brother Tom uses a planner.
He writes the date on every page.
Tom uses the computer screen and the keyboard.
Mia is tired, but she is happy.
dialogue: Noah, is this Mia's study desk?
Yes, it is. She uses a planner every day.
Nice. I use a notebook and my computer.
Her brother Tom types on the keyboard and looks at the screen.
Do you have a pencil? I want to write a note.
Yes, I have one. Here you are.
Thanks. Is Mia happy with her study desk?
Yes, she is. She studies there every day.

title: Estudando em grupo
grammar: We e they ao relatar o que grupos fazem
reading: Today we work outdoors at school.
I am in group one with Rosa and Tom, my classmates.
We sit at a big table under a tree.
They work together on a computer.
We are hungry, but we wait for lunch.
At two, both groups take a seat and share their work.
dialogue: Are we in the same group, Noah?
Yes, we are. We work together on page two.
Great. Where are our classmates this morning?
They are under that tree, near the big table.
Do they have a computer? We need a screen.
Yes, they have one. They wait for us.
Good. Please take a seat. We are hungry.
Yes, we are. We can eat after school.

title: Chegando com a mala
reading: Sam and Liz are at the station with their luggage.
Sam has a big suitcase, and it is heavy.
Liz has a small carry-on bag.
It is cold, and Sam has a new coat in his suitcase.
Liz has a computer and a planner in her bag.
They go to the beach, and they help each other.
dialogue: Hi Rosa! Is this your suitcase?
Yes, it is. I have a heavy suitcase.
Wow. Can I help you with the luggage?
Thanks. Do you have a carry-on bag too?
Yes, I have a small bag with my computer and planner.
Good. It is cold today. Do you have a coat?
No, but Mia has a new coat in her bag.
Great. Yes, we can go to the beach now.

title: O horário de fechamento do parque
grammar: What time does…? com verbos de funcionamento
reading: It is late, and Ana and Noah are outdoors in the park.
A sign by the gate shows the closing time.
The park closes at six, so they walk on the pathway.
Noah wants a hot drink before it closes.
A group of people comes to the park every day.
At six, a man says, “Please close the gate.”
dialogue: Excuse me. What time does the park close?
It closes at six. Now it is five thirty.
Only thirty minutes! Can we walk outdoors now?
Yes, we can. Is there a hot drink near the gate?
Yes, there is a small cafe. A group goes there every day.
Nice. What time does the cafe close?
At six too, I think. Can we have a hot drink?
Yes, we can. It is a good plan.

title: Quantos minutos até o lago?
grammar: How long para perguntar pela duração
reading: Ida and Leo are at the park entrance.
They want to see the lake before it closes.
A sign shows the closing time and the lake path.
The walking time is short: the lake is ten minutes away.
They walk on the pathway, and the water is near.
Soon they sit on a bench by the water.
dialogue: Excuse me. Is this the way to the lake?
Yes, it is. Walk on the pathway.
Thanks. How long does it take to walk there?
It takes ten minutes. Please read the sign here.
OK. The sign says the closing time is six.
Yes. Can we walk to the lake before it closes?
Sure. Is there a bench by the water?
Yes, there is. It is a nice place.

title: Confirmando a plataforma
reading: Pablo and Nina are at the station with a heavy suitcase.
There are three platforms, and the night train arrives soon.
Pablo has the tickets, but Nina has the luggage.
They ask a woman, “Which platform is for this train?”
She says, “Platform two, track four.”
They walk to platform two, and the train arrives in one minute.
dialogue: Excuse me. Which platform is for the night train?
Platform two. It arrives in five minutes.
Thank you. Which track is it? My suitcase is heavy.
Track four, near the big sign on the left.
Sorry, can you speak slowly, please?
Sure. Platform two, track four. Wait near the stairs.
Thanks. Is the night train on platform two now?
Yes, it is. It arrives in one minute.

title: Tomando notas para a aula
grammar: In e on para localizar o que foi escrito
reading: Kim sits at a desk with a pen and a heavy notebook.
She wants to take notes in class.
She writes the new word in her notebook.
The date goes on the first page, with the year.
Her birthday is on Friday, so she writes it in the notebook.
After a minute, she reads her notes on the train.
dialogue: Tom, where can I write the new word?
Write it in your notebook, Kim.
OK. And the date? The library closes soon.
Put the date on the first page. Then write the year.
Can I take notes with your pen, please?
Sure. Here you are. Your train arrives in a minute.
Thanks. Can I write my birthday in your notebook?
Yes, you can. Please write it now.

title: Informando o nome na recepção
reading: Ana walks into a hotel with her heavy suitcase.
She wants to check in at the front desk.
The hotel clerk asks, “What name is the reservation under?”
Ana says, “It is under my name, Ana Silva.”
The clerk gives her a pen and one page.
Then she gives Ana a room key.
dialogue: Hello! Are you here to check in?
Yes, I have a reservation for two nights.
What name is the reservation under, please?
It is under my name, Ana Silva.
Yes, I see it. Is your mother here too?
Yes, my mother and father are in the car.
Good. Take this pen, write your name on the page, and take the key.
Thank you! Yes, I have the key and my suitcase.

title: Subindo de elevador
reading: Mia and her sister Ana are at the hotel.
They check in at the front desk.
The hotel clerk gives Mia a key.
Her room is on the second floor.
Ana has a room on the first floor.
Mia pushes the button and the elevator comes.
dialogue: Hello, I want to check in under my name, Mia Lopes.
Welcome, Mia! Your room is on the second floor.
Great. Is the elevator near the front desk?
Yes, it is. Push the button and wait, please.
My sister has a room too. Is it on the second floor?
No, her room is on the first floor, near the lobby.
Really? Okay. I see the stairs. Can I use them?
Yes, you can. Here is your key, and have a nice day.

title: Lendo o número do assento
grammar: Ordinal para localizar assentos e fileiras
reading: Lia and her family take the train to the lake.
They arrive at platform two and get on.
Lia has a ticket for seat twelve.
Her seat is in the third row, by the window.
Her brother sits in the second row.
Lia looks at the number and smiles.
dialogue: Excuse me, I have a ticket for seat twelve.
Seat twelve is in the third row, by the window.
Thank you. Is my seat next to the door?
No, it is near the window. The first row is by the door.
Oh, I see the number now. My brother has seat eleven.
Seat eleven is in the second row, near your seat.
Okay. Can my brother and I sit together, please?
Yes, you can. Your family can sit together here.

title: Dizendo quando sai a próxima partida
grammar: The next + nome para identificar o próximo item
reading: Noah and his sister are at the station.
He looks at the display for the time.
The next train departs at three.
It is the red line, and it arrives at platform two.
A later train departs at four.
Noah and his sister wait there for the train.
dialogue: Excuse me, what time does the next train depart?
The next train departs at three. Look at the display.
Which line is it? I see the color red on the display.
It is the red line. It arrives at platform two.
Is there a later train? My sister wants to buy a snack.
Yes, there is. A later one leaves at four.
Great, we have time for a snack. Thank you!
No problem. Yes, the red line is at platform two.

title: Deixando um recado no papel
reading: Rosa is a hotel clerk at the front desk.
A man comes and wants to leave a message.
He takes a blue pen and a page of paper.
He writes his name and his phone number on the note.
The note says, "Please call back after six."
Rosa puts the note by the phone.
dialogue: Hello, Rosa. Can I leave a message for my friend?
Sure, Tom. Take a pen and write on this page.
What do I write on the page? I have his phone number.
Write this: Please call back after six.
Okay, I have the pen. Is blue fine for the note?
Yes, blue is fine. Please write your name big.
Done! Please give this note to my friend, Rosa.
Of course, Tom. The note is by the phone now.

title: Chegando cedo à clínica
grammar: Early, late e on time com be
reading: Iris has an appointment at the clinic at ten.
She is early today, and she is happy.
She takes the elevator to the second floor.
She checks in at the front desk.
The nurse says the doctor is not late.
Iris is tired, so she sits and waits.
dialogue: Hello, I want to check in. My appointment is at ten.
It is under your name. You are early, Iris.
Really? I am happy. Is the doctor on time today?
Yes, she is on time. Take the elevator to the second floor.
Good. I am tired, so I want to sit. Can I wait here?
Of course. Take a seat by the window. The nurse can call you.
Thank you. Can I call my sister on my phone?
Yes, you can. Please do not talk loud, okay?

title: Embarcando no trem
reading: Dan has a big bag and a ticket for the next train.
He is early, so he waits by the door.
The train stops, and the passengers get off.
Dan must wait for the passengers first.
Then he can board the train.
He puts his luggage by his seat in the third row.
dialogue: Excuse me, can I board the train now?
Not yet. The passengers must get off first.
Okay. Is this the next train on the display? I am early.
Yes, it is. Now you can board the train. Please use this door.
Do I show my ticket here? My luggage is big.
Yes, you must show your ticket at the door.
Here you are. Can I put my luggage by my seat?
Yes, you can. Your seat is in the third row.

title: Combinando uma caminhada
grammar: Would you like to + ação para convidar
reading: Jules wants to take a walk in the small park.
Ben is her walking partner.
She calls him in the morning.
They want to meet by the old tree.
They walk together and talk a lot.
Later, Ben has her phone number for the next walk.
dialogue: Hi, Ben! Would you like to walk with me?
Yes, I would. Where do you want to meet?
Can we meet in the park by the old tree?
Sure. Is it a small park or a big park?
It is a small park, and it is very nice.
Would you like to go early, at eight?
Eight is early for me. Can we walk together at nine?
Yes, nine is good. I have your phone number, Jules.

title: Mandando uma mensagem rápida
grammar: Present continuous para uma ação em andamento
reading: Ivan is outside the door, and it is cold.
He is typing a text message to Tess.
Tess is reading the new message on her phone.
She is sending a reply right now.
Tess types the next text and opens the door.
Later, they have hot tea in the kitchen.
dialogue: Hi, Tess! I am outside the door, and it is cold.
Oh no! I am reading your text message right now.
Good. Please send a reply, and then open the door.
I am sending my reply now. Wait a minute, Ivan.
Please hurry. My hands are cold, and I want to go in.
I am coming to the door right now.
Great! I am early, so I can wait here.
Yes, you are early. Come in, and have some hot tea.

title: Ligando para uma amiga
reading: Ana wants to call her friend Kim after school.
She uses her phone, and it rings two times.
A man answers, and she hears his voice.
Ana says her name and asks for Kim.
Kim is at home, and she comes to the phone.
Then the two friends talk about the park.
dialogue: Hello? Who is this, please?
This is Ana. Is Kim at home?
Yes, she is at home. Are you her friend?
Yes, I am her friend from school. I have a text message for her.
Wait a moment, please. She is in the kitchen.
Thank you. I want to meet her at the park later.
Hello, Ana! This is Kim. Can we meet right now?
Yes, we can. Please reply to my text message, Kim.
